record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.context_brief: Seymour conjecture for split and multipartite classes
record.original_question: Can Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture be verified for split oriented graphs and for multipartite tournaments? A split digraph has its vertices partitioned into a semicomplete part and an arc-less part, and a multipartite tournament is an orientation of a complete multipartite graph.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1 Verify that Seymour’s Conjecture holds for (a) split oriented graphs, (b) multipartite tournaments.
An orientation of a complete multipartite graph is called a multipartite tournament.
A split digraph D is a digraph in which vertices can be partitioned into two sets X and Y such that D[X] is a semicomplete digraph and D[Y ] is an arc-less digraph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A digraph is a directed graph without loops; an oriented graph is a digraph with no pair of mutually opposite arcs. A digraph is semicomplete if for every pair of distinct vertices u,v at least one of the arcs (u,v),(v,u) is present. A split digraph is a digraph D whose vertex set admits a partition V(D)=X∪Y such that the induced subdigraph D[X] is semicomplete and D[Y] is arc-less (has no arcs). A multipartite tournament is an orientation of a complete multipartite (undirected) graph.

For a vertex v of a digraph D, let N⁺(v) denote the set of out-neighbors of v, and let N⁺⁺(v) denote the set of vertices w ≠ v such that w ∉ N⁺(v) and there exists u ∈ N⁺(v) with (u,w) an arc of D. Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture asserts that every oriented graph D contains a vertex v with |N⁺⁺(v)| ≥ |N⁺(v)|.

Prove or disprove Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture in each of the following two restricted classes:
(a) split oriented graphs (oriented graphs that are split digraphs);
(b) multipartite tournaments.
artifact.status_search_result: The general Seymour second neighborhood conjecture remains open. For the two restricted classes, partial results are known: Seymour's conjecture has been verified for several subfamilies of split oriented graphs (e.g., when the semicomplete part induces a regular or almost-regular tournament, and via split–twin extensions), and there are results for related classes such as tournaments and oriented bipartite graphs, but the full statement for arbitrary split oriented graphs and for arbitrary multipartite tournaments has not been fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture for Oriented Graphs of Order at Most Seven and Split–Twin Extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Results show the conjecture holds for some families of oriented split graphs, in particular when Y induces a regular or almost regular tournament.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on split oriented graphs but not a full resolution.

status_evidence.title: Second neighborhood problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In 1990, Paul Seymour conjectured that in every oriented graph there exists a vertex whose second neighborhood is at least as large as its first neighborhood. The conjecture remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Seymour's conjecture is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: On Seymour's and Sullivan's Second Neighbourhood Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Seymour's and Sullivan's conjectures for oriented split graphs and related classes.
status_evidence.claim: Active research addresses the split case with only partial results.
